lessons.situation: A provider has been assigned after landlord approval and has made contact attempts with the tenant (a callback request and a failed call connection), but no booking has been confirmed and nothing in the contact requires an agency reply.
lessons.action: Review the provider's contact attempts to see whether they ask the agency for anything. If they only concern arranging access with the tenant and need no agency response, do not intervene or send new messages. Put the job on hold with the reason 'waiting for provider' and a note that the appointment is still to be booked, then let the provider and tenant sort out the visit and revisit if no booking is confirmed.
lessons.rationale: Provider-tenant call attempts are a normal part of scheduling and need no agency action, so holding with a clear note avoids duplicate chasing while keeping the job visible until the appointment is booked.

lessons.situation: A contractor has been asked to quote for an end-of-tenancy clean after the tenant vacated, and replies asking for the check-out report to be attached to the request so they can scope the work.
lessons.action: When a contractor quoting a check-out clean asks for the check-out report, locate the report on the property record and email it to that contractor on the same job thread, referencing the job ID, without escalating or pausing for a human handoff. Keep the job on hold awaiting their estimate.
lessons.rationale: The check-out report defines the cleaning scope and condition, so supplying it promptly is a routine information request that unblocks an accurate quote.

lessons.situation: A contractor has been assigned to a repair and left a voicemail for the tenant to arrange access, then the system prompts the operator to decide whether a response to the provider is needed or to return the job to auto mode.
lessons.action: Don't return the job to auto mode yet. Text the tenant (twice if needed) to say the contractor has tried to reach them and give the contractor's direct number so they can call back. Put the job on hold and ask the contractor by email, with a matching SMS nudge, whether the tenant has got back to them.
lessons.rationale: A voicemail alone doesn't confirm that a booking has been made, so nudging the tenant and checking in with the contractor keeps scheduling moving and stops the job stalling unnoticed in auto mode.

lessons.situation: A contractor assigned to a tenant-reported appliance repair has not confirmed an appointment despite several automated email and SMS reminders, then replies by email (content not captured) after the system flags that three or more reminders have gone unanswered.
lessons.action: When the contractor replies after repeated reminders, read the reply and check it gives a visit date and time slot agreed with the tenant. If it does, acknowledge it briefly, record the visit as confirmed or rescheduled with that date and slot, and send the contractor a single confirmation email with the slot, tenant contact details and a note that the tenant may request changes. Stop further chasers once the booking is confirmed. If the reply gives no date, ask the contractor for one.
lessons.rationale: Once the contractor has responded with a booking, the reminder cycle has done its job, and recording the confirmed slot and sending one clear confirmation stops redundant chasers and keeps the tenant, contractor and task status aligned.

lessons.situation: A lock repair has been completed by the contractor and confirmed by phone, the request is in final checks, and the system prompts the agent to decide whether the provider needs a reply or the request can go back to auto mode, while the contractor sends a routine email with appointment/job details.
lessons.action: Review the contractor's latest email and the call notes to confirm it is only routine confirmation or job detail and the work is already confirmed complete; if no question or action is outstanding, send no reply and return the request to auto mode. Meanwhile log the key handover (new key received, added to the key records and copied) and note that any missing completion documents were skipped because the job is complete, then proceed to the remaining closeout checks such as landlord confirmation.
lessons.rationale: Replying to routine contractor emails after the work is verified adds noise, so the agent should only intervene when something is outstanding and otherwise let automation handle closeout while the physical key and record-keeping steps are finished.

Dear Mrs Whitcombe,

8 Kestrel Lane, Fenwick, ZZ3 8ZZ – ref R/16

Sparkwell Electrical (NICEIC) have completed the EICR at the property and the result is UNSATISFACTORY:
- C2 (potentially dangerous): no RCD protection on the socket circuits
- C2 (potentially dangerous): scorched and loose neutral connection in the consumer unit (heat damage at the neutral bar)
- C3 (improvement recommended): no surge protection

The electrician recommends remedial work within 28 days, and sooner given the scorching. The tenant has also reported an unusual smell from the fuse box cupboard, so we have asked Sparkwell to attend urgently to check and make the installation safe – that is emergency safety work.

The proposed remedial work is to replace the consumer unit with RCD protection and test, at an estimated cost of approximately £620. We will send the written quote and the EICR as soon as we receive them.

Please reply APPROVE to go ahead with the consumer unit replacement up to £620, or DECLINE. A member of our team may also call you today given the urgency.

Kind regards,
Donna
Maintenance team

input.subject: Fuse box at 8 Kestrel Lane (R/16) – safety advice
input.body:
Dear Mr Brandt,

Thank you for letting us know about the smell – that's important. The electrician found a loose, heat-damaged connection in the fuse box (consumer unit) and the socket circuits don't have RCD protection, so we're treating this as urgent.

Until it has been checked:
- If you notice a burning smell, smoke, buzzing or crackling, or the unit feels hot, switch off the main switch at the fuse box only if you can do so safely, get everyone out and call 999 if there's smoke or fire.
- Keep the fuse box cupboard clear and don't store anything in or against it.
- Avoid running several high-power appliances at once (heaters, tumble dryer, kettle, oven), and unplug things not in use, especially overnight.
- Keep children away from the cupboard and check your smoke alarms work.

We've asked Sparkwell Electrical to come back urgently to check and make it safe, and they'll contact you to arrange a time – we've told them you're usually in after 3pm. We're also arranging the permanent repair with your landlord. We'll update you by tomorrow afternoon at the latest.

Kind regards,
Donna, Maintenance team
